newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares close mixed in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares close mixed in quiet trade.

text.p: Leading Russian shares closed mixed in quiet trade on Friday and traders said volumes were small after the U.S. Thanksgiving Day holiday.
"You can already feel pre-New Year tiredness," a trader said. "I would not take a long-term or a short-term position now, I can only see speculative possibilities."
The RTS-24 index slipped 0.28 percent to 187.90.

The International Monetary Fund said yesterday that it would start paying Russia tranches of its $10 billion loan in December, but traders said that the market was waiting for the actual payments before making decisions.
"Everything is waiting for what will happen in December," said German Zvezdin, equities salesman at Troika Dialog. "Actually everyone expected that."
The news that Russia intends to sell lots in state telecom holding company Svyazinvest to both Russian and foreign investors, starting early 1997, helped Rostelekom prices.
"There was renewed interest in Rostelekom," he said.
Russia had previously dropped N.M. Rothschild as organiser of the Svyazinvest sale and The Financial Times said Russia's Alfa-Bank and Most-Bank would handle the deal.
"Foreigners were waiting for a Russian inside deal, something like a new loans-for-shares scheme," Zvezdin said. "The news is good for the company, because the sale has to be open."
The government also plans to transfer its 38 percent stake, equal to 51 percent of the voting shares, in Rostelekom to Svyazinvest.
Rostelekom was $2.36 after $2.37 at Thursday's close.
Zvezdin forecast the market would open at Friday's close on Monday and would drift down until the New Year.

UES rose to $0.0820 from $0.0813, Mosenergo fell to $0.985 from $0.979, LUKoil edged up to $10.60 from $10.52, Yuganskneftegaz leapt to $9.50 from $6.35 in tiny volume and Gazprom fell to $0.340 from $0.353.
